transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-11-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Lucidity - Channel Lead), Sophie Martin (Lucidity - Alliance Manager), Karen Cho (Lucidity - BDR)

Summary:
Quick pipeline review between Redwood and Lucidity to align on co-sell motions, prioritise pilot accounts, and confirm next steps for security and pricing. Discussed potential conflicts with AWS Bedrock and timeline for pilots.

Topics:
- Current co-sell pipeline and stages
- Technical fit for two pilot accounts (low latency search and customer support)
- Pricing and margin splits for partner-led deals
- Security docs and SOC2 questions
- Next steps: spreadsheets, intros, engineer syncs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh Marcus Sophie Karen, appreciate you making time.
[00:06] Marcus Lee: Yeah thanks Jordan, excited to run through the pipe and see where we can accelerate a couple deals.
[00:12] Priya Shah: Hi all, Priya from Redwood, I'll be the technical touch on this one, want to make sure we've got the right pilot scoping.
[00:18] Sophie Martin: Awesome, quick note im on mobile so audio might be a little iffy.
[00:22] Karen Cho: same, on the road but i can hear fine.
[00:25] Jordan Ellis: Cool, quick agenda - 1) pipeline review 2) technical fit for the two pilots you flagged 3) pricing splits and enablement 4) next steps. Sound good?
[00:33] Marcus Lee: Yep, go ahead. The main thing for us is to fast track the search pilot with, um, NovaRetail and a second support automation pilot with Helix Health. Both are within a Q1 timeline.
[00:43] Jordan Ellis: Great, timeline wise Q1 works - are there any legal or procurement gating items already?
[00:49] Sophie Martin: Procurement's okay but security is the holdup, they want SOC2 and details on VPC/private deploy options. We already saw your SOC2 summary but the security lead wants a little deeper dive.
[00:59] Priya Shah: Totally, we can do a security deep-dive - Redwood Private lets you run a VPC control plane and we have KMS integrations. We'll get the detailed checklist to you.
[01:09] Karen Cho: For pricing - we usually resell at a markup, what's the typical margin you see for partner resell?
[01:15] Jordan Ellis: We try to be flexible, most partners aim for 15-25% on hosted deals; for Dedicated or Private there's more room since it's contract based. We can model a couple scenarios and i'll put them in the spreadsheet.
[01:26] Marcus Lee: Any overlaps with AWS Bedrock or Anthropic partnerships we should be aware of? Some of our customers already evaluate Bedrock as a baseline.
[01:33] Priya Shah: Yeah Bedrock is often the default, our angle is predictable latency and co-sell support - also easier to do dedicated pools and on-prem where needed. For Helix Health, the Private deployment is attractive for their PHI concerns.
[01:45] Sophie Martin: For NovaRetail, their key metric is 99th percentile latency under 200ms for ecomm search reranking. Can Redwood hit that on hosted?
[01:54] Priya Shah: On our hosted tier, for smaller sequence models we usually see p99 around 120-220ms depending on query patterns and batching. For strict 200ms SLO we might recommend a Dedicated pool or colocated infra; i'll put numbers in the estimate. There's also model quantization tradeoffs.
[02:10] Jordan Ellis: Perfect, can you run the two estimates - one hosted baseline and one dedicated - and include cost per 1k queries and expected p95/p99?
[02:19] Priya Shah: Yep i'll do that. I'll need some sample QPS and avg token lengths - Marcus can you share those?
[02:25] Marcus Lee: For NovaRetail we expect bursty traffic up to 40 qps during peak, avg query token length maybe 30-40, reranking model uses a context window around 64 tokens. For Helix Health support bot it's lower qps like 6-8, but sequences can be longer 200-400 tokens.
[02:41] Jordan Ellis: Good details. On the co-sell pipeline, Karen had previously uploaded a sheet, karen, any updates on stages?
[02:47] Karen Cho: Yeah i've updated NovaRetail to 'proposal' and Helix to 'POC scoping'. There's also a mid-market lead, Vertex Labs, that might be a smaller play.
[02:58] Marcus Lee: For the security intro, who should be the contact from Redwood?
[03:02] Jordan Ellis: Our security PM is Luis Ortega, he'll join the deep-dive; i'll intro him.
[03:07] Sophie Martin: And can we get an architecture diagram for Private deployment?
[03:11] Priya Shah: Yes i'll attach a diagram and a one-pager on network requirements; note sometimes the diagram references 'KV cache' as 'kay vee cache' in older docs - sorry for any audio artifact in docs.
[03:22] Marcus Lee: lol, we've seen that in transcripts.
[03:24] Jordan Ellis: Okay, on deal motion - if Lucidity leads with a reseller contract, what's the standard enablement package?
[03:31] Jordan Ellis: We typically include co-marketing credits, sales training session, and a 2-week technical onboarding window for pilots. For dedicated/private deals we do an onboarding SOW.
[03:40] Karen Cho: Training would be great. Also, any objection on exclusivity - some customers ask us to be exclusive for certain verticals.
[03:48] Priya Shah: We rarely do exclusivity; it's usually handled case-by-case and tied to significant commit.
[03:54] Marcus Lee: About competitive positioning, customers sometimes raise OpenAI as an easier dev experience. How do we address that?
[03:59] Jordan Ellis: Emphasize predictability and support, plus the ability to run private deployments for compliance. Also show cost per unit comparisons for typical request patterns.
[04:10] Sophie Martin: Can we get some client-facing benchmarks or a one-pager that we can redistribute?
[04:15] Jordan Ellis: Yes i'll share a one-pager and a short benchmark deck - i'll include hosted vs dedicated numbers.
[04:21] Priya Shah: Also a note on model versions - we recommend pinning model versions for pilots to avoid drift; Redwood's rollout tooling helps.
[04:29] Karen Cho: For Helix Health, they asked about data residency - we can host EU accounts in EU region, right?
[04:34] Priya Shah: Yes, we have EU regions and Private deployments can be entirely customer-managed.
[04:38] Marcus Lee: Great. Anything else on pipeline items?
[04:41] Karen Cho: i've added a note for Vertex Labs to do a short demo next week.
[04:45] Jordan Ellis: OK next steps recap: Jordan share pipeline spreadsheet with pricing, Priya provide two estimates and architecture doc, Marcus intro to security lead, Karen schedule the demo.
[04:56] Marcus Lee: i'll send the intro this week.
[04:59] Sophie Martin: thanks everyone.
[05:01] Jordan Ellis: Thanks, we'll follow up with items and set next meeting for two weeks.

End of transcript.
